overview: Model checkout as explicit states and guard transitions. Disable repeated submit while pending but also reuse one idempotency key for retries of the same attempt. Payment provider fields tokenize sensitive input; query order status after an ambiguous timeout before starting a new attempt. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

estimation.assumption: 100 cart lines; quantity edit changes 1 line and summary
estimation.calculation: 1 edited line + derived totals, rather than 100 independent total calculations
estimation.result: Memoize only profiled expensive work; authoritative totals still come from server
estimation.implication: Profile form input latency and payment-SDK loading on slow devices.

Payment provider fields tokenize sensitive input; query order status after an ambiguous timeout before starting a new attempt. Performance plan: Cart of up to 100 lines; delay payment SDK load until needed, avoid full-page rerenders on every keystroke. Accessibility: Native form labels and autocomplete attributes, inline error associations, focus first invalid field, step headings and an announced pending state. A visual spinner alone does not communicate submission. Failure recovery: Show pending confirmation, reuse checkoutAttemptId to query/retry safely; server verifies order ownership. Do not double-charge by generating a fresh attempt automatically. Trade-off: Optimistic quantity updates feel fast but need version reconciliation. Pessimistic final checkout is clearer where price and stock must be confirmed.

flows.title: Local interaction, state transition and UI update

steps.title: Receive user intent
steps.explanation: Edit cart quantities and reconcile authoritative totals. Native form labels and autocomplete attributes, inline error associations, focus first invalid field, step headings and an announced pending state. A visual spinner alone does not communicate submission.

steps.title: Apply the owning transition
steps.explanation: Model checkout as explicit states and guard transitions. Disable repeated submit while pending but also reuse one idempotency key for retries of the same attempt. Payment provider fields tokenize sensitive input; query order status after an ambiguous timeout before starting a new attempt.

steps.title: Render controlled child state
steps.explanation: Cart of up to 100 lines; delay payment SDK load until needed, avoid full-page rerenders on every keystroke. Child events return to the owner; focus and selection use stable identities.

steps.title: Capture user intent without duplicating authority
steps.explanation: Validate local input and enter a pending state. Use the component callback rather than mutating server snapshots directly.

steps.title: Send the versioned operation
steps.explanation: Call POST /checkout/attempts through the API adapter. Request: Idempotency-Key: checkoutAttemptId; {cartId,expectedVersion,addressId,paymentToken}. A prior successful response or unresolved operation must not be overwritten by a stale retry.

steps.title: Reconcile or expose recovery
steps.explanation: Show pending confirmation, reuse checkoutAttemptId to query/retry safely; server verifies order ownership. Do not double-charge by generating a fresh attempt automatically. Update the query key with the acknowledged version or invalidate/refetch it; maintain focus and make pending/error state visible.

failureCases.scenario: Payment succeeds but the order response is lost
failureCases.handling: Show pending confirmation, reuse checkoutAttemptId to query/retry safely; server verifies order ownership. Do not double-charge by generating a fresh attempt automatically.

failureCases.scenario: Route or identity changes while work is in flight
failureCases.handling: Dispose subscriptions, abort obsolete reads and ignore old generations; partition/clear private cache before showing a new account. Preserve only explicitly safe drafts.
